issue_context.title: Panasonic Viera integration error on start up
issue_context.body:

  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/

  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
Running beta 0.117.0b1 on restarting home assistant I receive this error:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.panasonic_viera
Source: components/panasonic_viera/__init__.py:96
Integration: Panasonic Viera (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 16:15:06 (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 16:15:06
Couldn't gather device info. Please restart Home Assistant with your TV turned on and connected to your network. 
```

This did not occur with 0.116.4


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.117.0b1
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.116.4
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): HassOS 4.14 
- Integration causing this issue: Panasonic Viera
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/panasonic_viera/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
Nil, set up in the UI.
```yaml

```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

When this television is off there is no network interface. So no wonder it has a problem, however in 0.116.4 this merely resulted in the state of the device being 'Unknown'.
comments:
I'm seeing similar errors:
```
2020-10-22 09:10:56 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.panasonic_viera.config_flow] Could not establish remote connection: <urlopen error [Errno 113] Host is unreachable>
```
But in this case I have it configured in YAML to use the **turn_on_action** option:
```yaml
panasonic_viera:
 host: <ip address>
 name: Living Room TV
 turn_on_action:
   - service: wake_on_lan.send_magic_packet
     data:
       mac: "<mac address>"
```
and it also results in a phantom discovery - a discovered Panasonic Viera shows under Integrations which can't be configured until the television is turned on (and then disappears with a "device already configured").

heyyy @tomlut. this error actually happens because the integration couldn't update the TV entity with the new device metadata support that is being added in the new version. to fix it, you could either try to restart home assistant with your TV turned on or just reconfigure the integration through the ui 😉

@joogps Is that the same reason for my error (`Could not establish remote connection: ... Host is unreachable>`) and the device discovery when starting up with the television off?

If it is, then I've restarted several times with the television on and I'm still getting the error and discovery every time I restart it when the television is off (I need to use YAML configuration as, as far as I known, that is the only way to configure the turn on action.)

@gadgetchnnel nope that's different, probably network-related... i'm adding the turn_on_action field to the config flow soon, but in the meantime you could try to clean your config entries file manually to see if you can remove it somehow...

also, are you in the beta?

> you could either try to restart home assistant with your TV turned on or just reconfigure the integration through the ui 😉

I just restarted with the tv tuned on (there was nothing to configure in the UI) and now the media player has disappeared from dev tools / states completely.

Edit 1: So I deleted the integration and restarted again.  Now it is not being discovered.

Edit 2: I was able to add it manually. Going to turn the tv off and restart and see what happens.

Edit 3: Now getting the error:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.media_player
Source: components/panasonic_viera/media_player.py:87
Integration: Media Player (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 19:29:29 (2 occurrences)
Last logged: 19:29:29

    Error adding entities for domain media_player with platform panasonic_viera
    Error while setting up panasonic_viera platform for media_player

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 310, in async_add_entities
    await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 378, in _async_add_entity
    device_info = entity.device_info
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/panasonic_viera/media_player.py", line 87, in device_info
    "model": self._device_info[ATTR_MODEL_NUMBER],
KeyError: 'modelNumber'
```

And the entity has disappeared again. Previous to this faffing about it jut went to the state unknown (due to the NIC powering down when off).

With the TV turned on, after a restart the integration shows this:

![Screenshot_2020-10-23 Configuration - Home Assistant](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10679300/97017394-477b2680-1567-11eb-8a2b-a8b062746324.png)

But zero entities/devices have been created.

Edit 4: Oh joy. Not even deleting the UI integration and defining a YAML configuration works now. No entity created. And yes the IP address is correct.
@tomlut I think the integration is crashing because your model returns no model number in the metadata... i'm working on a pull request rn and I'll address this
Is there a curl command I can issue to check the metadata for you?

you could try to use the [Panasonic Viera library](https://github.com/florianholzapfel/panasonic-viera) to write a script and get the device info, or try to access it from your tv's upnp descriptor file http://\<ip-address\>:55000/nrc/ddd.xml

I'm also adding it as a logger debug item during setup now

OMG! Wait, you're adding remote commands too?

I have two devices left that rely on IR control. My projector - that I have plans to control via RS232, with actual state feedback, and this old but perfectly good Viera plasma tv. I was only looking at the Viera API last week. I had plans to add many rest commands, but am guessing this will no longer be required? Woohoo!

There's still the issue of no "on" command (who turns the NIC off IMO?) but I am going to whip up either an HDMI CEC ESP control board or just optocouple an ESP gpio across the (soft) power switch.

If it helps in any way this is the response I got from that URL.

```
10 urn:panasonic-com:device:p00RemoteController:1 VIERA ST50 Series Panasonic Panasonic VIErA uuid:4D454930-0200-1000-8001-CC7EE7D55111 uuid:4D454930-0100-1000-8001-CC7EE7D55111 uuid:4D454930-0200-1000-8001-CC7EE7D55111 NRC-2.00 DTV PAL-6,PAL-1 VR_DMR,VR_GPAD,VR_VECTOR,VR_BROWSER image/png 48 48 24 /nrc/dlna_icon_48.png image/png 120 120 24 /nrc/dlna_icon_120.png image/jpeg 48 48 24 /nrc/dlna_icon_48.jpg image/jpeg 120 120 24 /nrc/dlna_icon_120.jpg urn:panasonic-com:service:p00NetworkControl:1 urn:upnp-org:serviceId:p00NetworkControl /nrc/sdd_0.xml /nrc/control_0 /nrc/event_0
```

Model: THP60ST50A (not part of the response).

@tomlut yep, I was going to add it back in may but my plan was interrupted by some weird problems that started happening with some models. the code was just sitting there on my repo and now I'm finally pulling it in, haha

so yeah, apparently your descriptor file has no model number (which is a shame since I thought it would work universally), but i implemented a workaround for it in the new branch: setting default values - in this case, the model would just default to "Panasonic Viera")

actually it would be dope if you could download that branch and test it locally!
not only it would make the process of approval and merge faster but we would be able to detect any other issues too
I'm willing to try. I just have no idea how to.

essentially you just need to download [this repository](https://github.com/joogps/core/tree/panasonic-viera-remote) and open it within a Docker container. and then, of course, starting home assistant with the `hass` command, accessing it (https://localhost:8123), configuring and setting up the integration

>  open it within a Docker container.

This assumes much knowledge with docker that I do not have. If I get a chance I'll give it a go.

@tomlut it depends on the model. the one I have just goes offline when turned off, so there's nothing we can do unless making the tv unavailable. some other models stay connected, but that actually involves another problem (that I've already tried to debug but I couldn't), where the entity stays turned on forever, hahah

Mine is definitely turning on (and off) now. The TV is currently off so I just tried pinging the TV and got no response, but I can definitely control it from the integration. 

This is unexpected but wonderful news. Just going to have one more look through my config to make sure I don't have a turn_on action hidden somewhere in YAML.

EDIT: nope no turn_on action. No panasonc YAML at all. I commented out the IR remote TV power commands and restarted to be sure and still have control. Maybe my tv just does not respond to ICMP when off?
